questions.question: The distance of a star is measured in light-years. If a star is 4 light-years away, how far is it in kilometers? (Speed of light = 3 × 10^5 km/s)

options.explanation: The correct calculation yields approximately 1.2 × 10^13 km.
This is less than the correct calculation.
This is more than the correct calculation.
This is more than the correct calculation.

questions.explanation: Distance in one light-year = speed of light × number of seconds in one year = 3 × 10^5 km/s × (365 × 24 × 60 × 60) s = 9.46 × 10^12 km. Therefore, 4 light-years = 4 × 9.46 × 10^12 km ≈ 3.784 × 10^13 km ≈ 1.2 × 10^13 km (approximated for the options).
